info.title: BigFatFile API
info.description: The one public API of a BigFatFile Origin.

get.description:
Returns what the sign-in and sign-up screens offer on this server.

- `signUp` says whether anyone can create an account, or only people with an invitation.
- `providers` lists the external accounts that people can sign in with, such as Google or Microsoft.

Returns a token that protects against cross-site request forgery (CSRF). In that attack, another website makes the browser send a request, and the browser adds the session cookie to it.

- Send the token in the `X-CSRF-Token` header of every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE request that uses the session cookie.
- Get a new token after signing in or out, because each token belongs to one user.
- Requests with a bearer token do not need it.

post.description:
Checks the email address and the password, and starts a session. The response sets the session cookie.

The session works in one tenant. It is the tenant in `tenantId` when the request has one. Otherwise it is the tenant that the user signed in to last.

Errors:

- 401 with the code `wrong_credentials`: the address or the password is wrong.
- 403 with the code `email_not_confirmed`: the address is not confirmed yet.
- 403 with the code `locked_out`: the account is locked for 5 minutes, because of 10 wrong passwords in a row. During the lock, even the right password gets this answer.
- 404: the user is not a member of the tenant in `tenantId`.
- 429 with the code `too_many_requests`: this IP address made more than 20 sign-in attempts in one minute, for any accounts. The `Retry-After` header says how many seconds to wait. All the addresses of one IPv6 /64 block count as one address.

Ends the session and removes the session cookie.

The request must send the `X-CSRF-Token` header. Without it, the answer is 400 with the code `csrf_token_invalid`.

put.description:
Moves the session to another tenant that the user is a member of. The response sets a new session cookie, so every open tab of the web app switches too.

Answers 404 when the user is not a member of that tenant.

post.description:
Creates an account with a name, an email address and a password.

- With `invitationToken`, the invitation email proves that the person receives mail at the address. The account is created at once, joins the invited tenant, and its session starts. The outcome is `signed_in`.
- Without it, a confirmation email is sent. The account can sign in once the address is confirmed. The outcome is `confirmation_sent`.
- When the address already has an account, the outcome is also `confirmation_sent`, and that account gets an email saying so. This way the response does not reveal which addresses have accounts.

Errors:

- 400 with field errors: a field is not valid, for example a password shorter than 12 characters.
- 403 with the code `sign_up_closed`: this server accepts sign-ups only with an invitation, and the request has none. The one exception is the operator's address, set in `BFF_OPERATOR_EMAIL`.

Confirms the address with the user ID and the code from the confirmation email, and starts a session. The link in the email opens the web app, which reads both values from it.

On a server with open sign-up, this is also when the person's new tenant is created.

Answers 400 with the code `invalid_code` when the code is wrong or has expired.

Sends the confirmation email again, to an address that is not confirmed yet.

The answer is always 202, whether or not the address has an account. This way the response does not reveal which addresses have accounts.

Sends an email with a link to reset the password.

The answer is always 202, whether or not the address has an account. This way the response does not reveal which addresses have accounts.

Sets a new password, with the user ID and the code from the password reset email. The link in the email opens the web app, which reads both values from it.

Errors:

- 400 with the code `invalid_code`: the code is wrong or has expired.
- 400 with field errors: the new password is not valid, for example shorter than 12 characters.

get.summary: Sign in with an external account
get.description:
Sends the browser to the sign-in page of another service, such as Google or Microsoft. When the person has signed in there, the browser comes back to `returnUrl`, which must be a path on this server.

- `provider` is a `key` from `GET /account/options`.
- The web app opens this address as a page in the browser, not with a fetch call, because the browser must follow the redirects.

Answers 404 when this server has no provider with that key.

post.description:
Returns what an invitation is for, so that the invitation screen can show it before the person accepts: the tenant, who sent it, the invited address and the role.

- `accountExists` tells the screen whether to ask the person to sign in or to sign up.
- The token is sent in the request body, so it stays out of request logs.

Answers 404 when the token is unknown, has expired, was revoked or was already accepted.

Adds the signed-in user to the invited tenant, with the invited role. The session then works in that tenant.

Errors:

- 404: the token is unknown, has expired, was revoked or was already accepted.
- 409 with the code `wrong_account`: the user's email address is not the one the invitation was sent to.

get.description:
Returns the user that the token or session belongs to, and:

- `tenantId`: the tenant that the token or session works in;
- `tenants`: every tenant the user is a member of, with the user's role in each.

Answers 403 with the code `user_required` when the token has no user. An App that got a token for itself, with client credentials, has no user.
Returns the tenant's name, its plan and when it was created.
Returns the tenant's members, ordered by name, one page at a time.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The nextCursor of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return. The default is 100.

patch.description:
Changes the role of one member of the tenant.

Errors:

- 404: the user is not a member of the tenant.
- 409 with the code `last_admin`: the change would leave the tenant without an admin.

delete.description:
Removes a user from the tenant. The user loses access at once, also through tokens issued earlier.

Errors:

- 404: the user is not a member of the tenant.
- 409 with the code `last_admin`: the user is the tenant's last admin.

get.description:
Returns the invitations that nobody has accepted yet, newest first, one page at a time.

It needs the `members.manage` scope, because the invited addresses belong to people who are not members yet.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The nextCursor of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return. The default is 100.

post.description:
Invites an email address to the tenant with a role, and sends the invitation email. The link in the email works until `expiresAt`.

Inviting the same address again replaces the earlier invitation and sends a new email.

Errors:

- 400 with field errors: the address or the role is not valid.
- 409 with the code `already_member`: the address belongs to a member of the tenant.

delete.description:
Revokes an invitation. The link in its email stops working.

Answers 404 when the invitation does not exist or was already accepted.

code.description: The code from the password reset email.

name.description: The name to show on the button.

tenantId.description: The tenant to scope the session to. Without it, the session gets the tenant the user signed in to last.

SignUpOutcome.description: `confirmation_sent`: a confirmation email is on its way. It is also the answer when the address already has an account, so the response does not reveal which addresses do. `signed_in`: the invitation proved the address, the account exists and its session has started.

SignUpPolicy.description: `invitation`: only people with an invitation can create an account. `open`: anyone can create an account, and gets a new tenant of their own.

invitationToken.description: The token from an invitation email. It proves the address, so no confirmation email is sent.

plan.description: The plan's key. The open core has one plan, `unlimited`.

TenantRole.description: What a member may do in a tenant; node permissions apply on top. `admin` manages members, invitations and the tenant's settings. `guest` is an outside person who sees only what is shared with them.

oauth2.description: Tokens from this server's OpenID Connect endpoints. The web app on the same origin uses its session cookie instead.

session.description: The web app's session, on the same origin only. Write operations that use it must also send the X-CSRF-Token header, with the token from GET /account/csrf. A write operation without that header gets 400 with the code csrf_token_invalid.

tags.name: auth
tags.description:
The endpoints behind the web app's account screens: sign-up, sign-in, passwords and invitations.

- Only the web app calls them, from the same origin as the server.
- They work with the session cookie, not with tokens.
- Apps get their tokens from the OpenID Connect endpoints under `/connect` instead.

tags.name: tenant
tags.description:
The signed-in user, the tenant, its members and its invitations.

- A token or a session works in one tenant. A request with any other tenant's ID gets 404, the same answer as for a tenant that does not exist.
- The endpoints that need the `members.manage` scope are for admins only. A user who is not an admin of the tenant gets 403 with the code `admin_required`.
